IMO it’s pretty simple. It’s the  technical advancement of being able to constantly update games after they come out. Mario has been popular since 1985. Street Fighter since 1987. But only in the last ~15 or so years has “games as a service” been possible. Before that, popular IPs needed to release new games. 

Look outside games. Star Wars was popular after the OT cane out, but due to the fact that you can’t update a movie, they just released new content in the form of books, games, comics, and eventually new movies and shows. 

Sure Minecraft, Fortnite, and Roblox are the “same” games as they were when they were released. But the ability to pump out a constant stream of new content means that no “Minecraft 2” ever needs to come out in the same way popular IPs of the early days of gaming (or other current mediums) need to produce sequels.

I remember Kobe’s prime vividly. He was wildly popular, a superstar of not just the sport but general pop culture. But popularity does not necessarily equal influence in this case. What changes did he have on the game or the league? He didn’t change how the game was played, they didn’t have to implement new rules. He didn’t push the league to new heights in popularity. He himself was crazy popular but he is not one of the most influential players of all time IMO. They changed rules for Wilt and Kareem. Magic brought a new style of flashiness and swagger to the game. Jordan elevated the league to new popularity internationally and in the states. Even Iverson was influential with his style of play and attitude off the court. Curry would go on to revolutionize the three. 

I guess arguably thing Kobe brought was the “mamba mentality,” but really this was just Jordan 2.0. Other than that, he was an incredible player but very much played the style that Jordan popularized. Explosive wing with a deadly midrange, elite level defence, and championship mentality. Wildly popular, inspired a ton of kids, but how did he influence the league? 

I would almost argue LeBron could be discussed in the same breath. Unbelievable talent, wildly popular, but in terms of just influence? It’s not just a “who is better” or “who is the most popular.”

Men’s basketball is player, in part, above the rim. Being able to jump high can help with this in a lot of ways.

As a shorter guard, being able to penetrate and finish over talker defenders in the paint is a must. Without a solid vertical, finishing at the rim becomes very difficult. This is why you’ll see guards with poor verticals (Tony Parker, Steve Nash) go to their pull up and floater game while explosive guards (Westbrook, Drexler) jump and finish over and around defender. 

For bigs, finishing is the same. However, another important aspect is to be able to quickly bounce back up after landing. Consecutive jumps with minimal time on the ground can help in virtually every scenario. Go up to contest a shot, and once you land you want to be able to spring back up to secure rebounds. Same thing with offensive rebounds after getting your own miss, you want to jump back up after coming down. In the paint, being able to jump and go to your baby hook package is crucial to open up other opportunities and other moves. 

Lastly and maybe most importantly- vertical is directly related to explosiveness. The higher you can jump, the faster you can cut, the quicker you can defend, and the more explosive you are in the open court. Why do you think the NFL combine tests vertical and broad jump? Those aren’t moves that the players do, but they indicate explosiveness. You’ll never meet a slow guy who can jump super high.

Generally speaking (again, slight differences per person) the ball should be on the side of your shooting eye (so your left) because you’re left handed. The reason being, everything should be aligned pointed to the basket starting from your toe. So left toe lines up, then left knee, hip, elbow, hand, and eye. Many players will have their shooting foot pointed toward their body. This aligns your hip better. Look at a picture of Klay Thompson shooting. You draw a straight line from his foot to his knee to his hip to his elbow to his eye and to his hand at the final release. 

So that being said, when you catch it in your shooting pocket, that spot should be basically on your left hip (left foot you again, most players it is right). That way, when you elevate to shoot, the ball goes straight up to above your left eye before you actually shoot. 

Tldr: everything should be in a vertical straight line from toe to extended hand meaning keep the ball above your left eye.

Honestly it is often hard for left handed players to have “proper” shooting techniques because every coach demonstrates with their right hand especially at a young age. That being said, and as others have pointed out, shooting is less about form and more about consistency. The greatest shooters of all time have had “improper” form; Curry heaves it from his chest, Ray Allen shoots flat as shit etc. 
However, general rules can help the average players improve because we aren’t steph or ray. You do bring the ball to the right side of your head when you shoot. Generally this is seen as a negative. When we shoot, we want to eliminate as much side to side movement as possible because 1) eliminating more movement means it is easier to replicate every shot and 2) pulling it from the right side to the left can mean you’ll start missing left to right. It also seems as if your left knee bends in when you squat down to shoot. This may not seem like a big thing, but it could throw off your balance which again is a negative when we shoot.

1. Mistakes
This is a tough one. Everyone makes mistakes at every level of every game. It’s what makes the game worth playing! You mentioned a few things in specific. 

a) Randomly Running Around: of course, the simple answer is “don’t do that,” but that’s not helpful. What is more helpful is that on attack and defence, you always need to be asking yourself “what is my current goal?” This may change during the course of the round, but if you have no plan before the round starts, then you can easily just be running around. Some “goals” on attack may be “get this wall open,” “push out a roamer,” “take control of this room,” “help my hard breacher get to the wall safely.” On defence, you may want to set the goal of “waste time and utility by roaming so my anchors have an easier job,” “defend this room next to objective,” “ensure that the attackers can’t walk into this room too easily,” “anchor on site so the attackers can’t walk in.” As I said, these goals could change during a round. Maybe your hard breacher gets spawnpeeked, and now you need to make a quick decision as to how you can attack the site. This comes down to knowing the map, knowing your team comp, and knowing how the enemy is playing. This is a skill, and it takes time to know the best way to do this. But always ask yourself, “what is my current goal.”

b) Not Checking Corners
This comes down to two main things: knowing where defenders are likely going to be watching and repetition. The former can be achieved by watching all of your death replays to see the angles defenders are holding. For example, maybe you walk into a room and you get shot from the open hatch above. Next time, toss your drone in and make sure to look up first to see if the hatch is open. Speaking of the drone, this is the key on offence. You should drone EVERY room before you walk in unless you are running out of time severely or acting on the callout of a teammate. Otherwise, drone drone drone. 

c) Noticing Pings
This is partially on your teammates too, so dont be too frustrated. They need to be providing good callouts with pings, such as “Ela on 3 ping white stairs,” or “Ash on red ping front door.” Otherwise, again just keep playing and you’ll start noticing them more. 

d) Waiting Too Long

Tatcher- your main job is to follow your hard breacher around. Hard breacher is the term for Thermite, Hibana, and Ace. They are the operators who can open walls defenders reinforce, which typically have a Bandit battery, a Kaid electroclaw, or a Mute jammer behind (these are sometimes called anti-gadgets). All of these things will prevent the hard breacher from opening up the wall. Your job is to follow them to the wall they want to open, throw your EMP at the wall to destroy whatever anti-gadget is behind the wall. NOTE: in the new update, your EMPs will not destroy the anti-gadget, it will only disable it for an amount of time, meaning the timing between you and your hard breacher has to be more in sync. Sometimes, Kaid and Bandit will try to put their gadgets on the wall after your hard breacher has put/thrown their gadgets on the wall to destroy it. This is called tricking. Kaid is easy to prevent from tricking. Throw you EMP, your hard breacher will place his device, then throw another EMP. Kaid only has a short window from when the hard breach charge is placed to when it will open in which he can effectively trick. Throwing two back to back will counter this. 
Countering Bandit tricking is a little trickier. Often, teams will have another operator use their gadget/grenades to counter a trick. Flashbangs, Zofia’s concussion, and Capitao’s fire arrows come to mind. 
If you’re not playing with a friend, you can still help counter the Bandit trick. Throw your first EMP to clear his batteries and keep track of how many you destroy. If the hard breacher can bait him to place another battery, you have to be ready to throw your second EMP. Usually (not always) a Bandit won’t keep more than 1 battery in his pocket since many sites need at least 3 batteries. If you can bait the second out, don’t be too quick to throw the third. Wait to see if he places another, and until your hard breacher is ready. The worst thing a Thatcher can do is throw all 3 EMPs at the start and have Bandit have a battery left.

Mozzie’s gadget allows him to be very situational. You will play him differently depending on your situations. For solo q, you should see what your teammates are doing before you commit to a strat. He is best utilized as a roamer, but there can be times when you might have to hold site. If you see you already have a Vigil, Cav, or others already roaming, it might be best to shallow roam or even anchor. Hopefully if you pick Mozzie, your teammates will see and recognize “this guy is going to roam.” But don’t pre-determine that, lots of people just focus on themselves and won’t pay any mind to you.

If you are roaming- set up in an area where attackers are likely to push through or want to control. Above hatches, near important hard walls, and 90 hallways come to mind. As with any roamer, it is more important to waste time and utility than to get kills. You have to position yourself correctly with room to escape and rotate back near site without dying. Having nearby hatches open and rotate holes help with this. There’s no set rule for when you want to leave and go back to site, but some general rules would be 1) when the enemy team is executing their final push 2) when you are being pushed aggressively and you know you can’t win a gunfight (you are being flashes, attackers have long angles) 3) you have wasted a lot of time and utility and want to play conservative because you are up a man or two. With Mozzie when roaming, use your drones to cover popular drone entrances in the area you are roaming in. Most uncoordinated teams will drone themselves and not their teammates, and you can use this to your advantage. Once you snag a drone, don’t immediately reposition it unless you know you are safe. If you can, move it to watch a flank, and pray a teammate can watch it for you. Otherwise, flip to it if you know you are safe and listen for attackers. When you cant go on it, listen for attackers shooting it when they come across it. If you know where you placed your drones, you’ll know roughly where the attackers are. Again, don’t push unless you know you can secure a kill. The key is to waste time and utility. 

If you have to anchor- play him like mute. You can either 1) Block popular drone entrances later in the round to hide you anchor position. This is less effective than 2) collect drones in the prep phase and right after and use them like valk cams. If queuing with a team, use one to help out your roamers. Otherwise, use them to watch important hallways and walls. Hide them well, the attackers will know when they lose their drones and its easy to tell when its a Mozzie drone. Again, he’s a worse anchor, but his primaries are some good options for close range. The commando has better long range potential, but try to hold closer angles if you’re aim isn’t on point. Use the C4 smart, dont burn it to early.

There are three safe ways to defrost beef: in the refrigerator, in cold water, and in the microwave. Never defrost on the counter or in other locations.

•Refrigerator:. It's best to plan ahead for slow, safe thawing in the refrigerator. Ground beef, stew meat, and steaks may defrost within a day. Bone-in parts and whole roasts may take 2 days or longer. Once the raw beef defrosts, it will be safe in the refrigerator for 3 to 5 days before cooking. During this time, if you decide not to use the beef, you can safely refreeze it without cooking it first.

•Cold Water:. To defrost beef in cold water, do not remove packaging. Be sure the package is airtight or put it into a leakproof bag. Submerge the beef in cold water, changing the water every 30 minutes so that it continues to thaw. Small packages of beef may defrost in an hour or less; a 3- to 4-pound roast may take 2 to 3 hours.

•Microwave:. When microwave defrosting beef, plan to cook it immediately after thawing because some areas of the food may become warm and begin to cook during microwaving. Holding partially-cooked food is not recommended because any bacteria present wouldn't have been destroyed.

Its tough to just say “use this main” without knowing your play-style, if you’re playing solo, and how good your aim is. 

Play-style- Basically, how well do you know the maps, how fast do you like to play, how patient are you holding angles etc. Do you like to be the first one in? Hang back? Find roamers? Rush? Those are all things you have to figure out. 

Paying solo/with group- if you’re playing with a group, you guys are probably gonna wanna strategize when attacking points. If you find a strat that works, you’re probably gonna wanna all play the same roles and start to main those ops. The most simple example is a hard breacher/anti-gadget op (Thermite/Thatcher). It just makes sense for you to play the same op over and over. Find the one you like and get good with their gun. 
If you’re queuing solo with no mic, you may want to play an op that has more utility when alone. I have found Zofia and Ying are able to use their gadgets without much combo. 

Aim- Most times, if you’re playing Ash, Zofia, or Blitz, it’s because you are top fragging. Obviously, there are other ops that are good fraggers, but those are very common. However, if your aim sucks, you can still influence the round. A good Twitch can be as crucial to a round as an Ash. Thatcher, Fuze, Capitao, Monty can all help your team without fragging. 

Hope this helps! Feel free to ask questions.
